items.narrative:
This audit covers 47 supply-chain events recorded between 2025-02-05 and 2025-06-15 across 14 products and 6 external trading partners. Of those 14 products, 5 are definitively on the Food Traceability List, 6 are classified as suspicious and require formal determination, and only 3 are confirmed off-list. The 47 events span seven critical tracking event types—cooling (3), first land-based receiving (3), harvesting (6), initial packing (6), receiving (6), shipping (19), and transformation (4)—giving a broad but uneven footprint that shipping activity dominates.

The most pressing gaps are the 8 high-or-medium findings flagged as scope or exemption uncertainty, meaning the business cannot yet confirm which regulatory obligations apply to nearly half its product portfolio; this is the single largest finding category and carries direct compliance risk. Seven findings are rated high severity in total, and 5 inbound ERP mismatches indicate that what the system records does not match what was actually received—a foundational data-integrity problem. Key data element coverage sits at 93.88%, with 27 missing data elements out of 441 graded, and 6 kde-completeness findings confirm those gaps are not isolated. Lot integrity is also strained: 2 backward-lineage gaps, 2 date-ordering anomalies, 2 duplicate traceability lot code issues, 2 mass-balance discrepancies, 1 forward-linkage gap, and 1 self-receive anomaly collectively undermine the chain of custody across 13 linked lots. Three GS1-related findings—1 identifier and 3 requirement issues—add further structural risk, and the traceability plan itself carries 1 open finding.

The immediate priority is to resolve the 8 scope-or-exemption-uncertainty findings by conducting a formal Food Traceability List classification review for all 6 suspicious products before any other remediation work, since the required records differ materially depending on that determination. The 5 inbound ERP mismatches must be reconciled event by event to establish a clean receiving baseline. Both Band D partners—METROGROCERSINC (11 events) and SUNBELTRESTAURANTSGROUP (8 events)—must be engaged directly with data-quality scorecards, as their band rating signals systemic deficiencies despite showing a fill rate of 1.0, which may reflect structural rather than completeness problems. The 27 missing key data elements should be mapped back to their source sheets and corrected before the next data pull, and the 2 backward-lineage gaps require supplier documentation to close the chain of custody on the 2 affected lots.
